questions.question: What can help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best protection against injury on a motorcycle. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face during a crash.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance for a motorcycle under normal conditions?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Use a larger distance when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: What should you do when railroad crossing lights are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Turn around and find an alternate route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at a railroad crossing with flashing lights. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to go around a train.

questions.question: Where is the greatest danger of conflict with other vehicles?
questions.explanation: Most conflicts between motorcycles and other vehicles happen at intersections. The biggest danger is when cars turn left in front of motorcycles.

questions.question: Which surface may have poor traction?
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet or icy pavement, gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on good pavement, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly re-apply the brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you have stopped completely.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks on good pavement, keep it locked until you stop. You can still control your motorcycle if it stays upright and goes straight.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Move to a different lane to give an emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: How does carrying a passenger affect stopping and speeding up?

options.text: Less time than usual to stop and speed up.
The same amount of time to stop and speed up as it usually does.
More time than usual to stop and speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: More time than usual to stop and speed up.
questions.explanation: Extra weight slows down acceleration and braking. Your motorcycle responds more slowly when carrying a passenger.

questions.question: What should you do if you get a flat tire while riding?

options.text: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
Shift your weight toward the good wheel and brake normally.
Brake on the good wheel while immediately pulling off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handle grips firmly and stay off the brakes.
questions.explanation: Grip the handlebars firmly and stay in a straight line. Avoid braking unless you know which tire is flat. Slow down and exit the road safely.

questions.question: How should a passenger sit on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put their feet on the ground when the motorcycle is stopped.
Not ride without a back rest.
Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit as far forward as possible without crowding the operator.
questions.explanation: Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the driver. Keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: If you wear a jacket while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool.
Keep the jacket on to protect you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you.
questions.explanation: A good riding jacket protects you in a crash, no matter how hot it is. Jackets also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Most motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet while riding a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when on a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally ride in which formation?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation allows a group to stay close while giving each rider enough space to ride safely. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and block your view.

questions.explanation: Mirrors alone are not enough to see everything around you. Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. This improves your view and helps drivers in the next lane see what you are doing.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while you stop on a straight road, what happens?

options.text: You must release the rear brake to regain control.

questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks while stopping on a straight road, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can usually control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing another vehicle on the left.

questions.question: A motorcycle must have all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: In Wyoming, a motorcycle must have: at least one headlight, one taillight, one brake light, one red rear reflector, a left-side mirror, a muffler, and a horn. Turn signals are optional.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The driver may need your lane to pass other cars.
You may be hidden in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have more escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be hidden in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous because the driver cannot see you in their blind spot. If something goes wrong, the vehicle may also block your way to escape.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding?
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you. Even in daylight, bright clothing helps. Reflective materials are also helpful.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often the person usually drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the person usually drinks
questions.explanation: BAC depends on body weight, how much alcohol is consumed, and how fast it is consumed. How often someone drinks does not affect BAC. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you cannot see clearly, or when traffic is heavy and cars may cut in front of you.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road splits into two separate lanes.
